Hi, so @empress thought you ladies may be interested in hearing a bit about my mom. So here's what I remember with some help from my older sister (my mom died in a car accident when I was 12). Hopefully you find this useful and helpful, if not, feel free to remove.

She loved her family very, very much and we were the center of her world. A typical school day would be as follows:

We would get up and dressed (clothes laid out the night before) make our beds and go down for breakfast,which was usually something simple but good and nutritious (oatmeal and a banana,or scrambled eggs ) We took care of the animals (that was our main chore, feeding and letting the dogs out and cleaning the cats litterbox and so on) and went to school

My older sister walked or rode bikes with friends to school, my mom walked me to mine most days and drove us when the weather was bad. lunches were mostly made the night before and were simple (turkey or pb&j sandwiches with fruit and yogurt or sometimes cheese sticks) she didn't like school lunches.

When we got home we were expected to do our homework before anything else (playing with friends, video games, tv). Many times we would sit in the kitchen and do our homework while our mom got our lunches ready for the next day and began dinner. She would ask us about our homework and help us if needed. We also had to walk the dogs and feed them before going anywhere

She was a good cook and always made sure dinner was ready when my dad got home. She would let us help her make cookies or brownies or pies from scratch sometimes on the weekends which of course we loved.

Once we were at school she did her routine, she would do different laundry on different days (sheets one day, towels the next, etc) and different cleaning different days as well (bathrooms one day, vacuuming one day, sweeping and mopping the next)

We were expected to keep our rooms tidy (things picked up from the floor , make our beds, as we got older clean our bathroom)and occasionally help with the dishes.

Structure was important (set bedtimes, limits on tv and so on) and we had different activities as well (ballet, soccer ). She would discipline us if needed although our dad was the main disciplinarian (wait until your father gets home struck fear in us)

Manners were stressed ,we were taught to respect our elders called our friends parents ma'am and sir and Mr and Mrs. (Last name). Always ask to be excused from the table and thank them for having us over. Thank you notes were sent after every Christmas and birthday to the relatives that sent gifts, and also to friends parents if something special happened (got taken along on an overnight trip to NYC , or camping)

She was a good sewer and made our bedspreads and curtains and lots of stuffed animals. (I still have 2) she taught my sister and tried to teach me although I was always a bit awkward, though I have fond memories of laying underneath her sewing table and reading a book.

She did the shopping and meal planning on Saturday, rarely did she forget something and when she did she would "sneak"us a little money for a treat for walking to the store (when we were older) or wed walk with my dad. Candy and other junk food was an occasional treat as was soda. I don't recall her really working out, but with healthy meals and no junk food she was always slender as were we.

She was sweet and kind. My sister was much more "girly" and wore dresses and played with dolls and makeup, I was always a bit more tomboyish and liked exploring outside. I say this because while I know she would rather I wore dresses, she accepted and loved me for who I was.

Her values and morals live on in us, although we lost her too early I am forever grateful that we had her.
I'm so sorry about your family losing your mother; you mom sounded freaking epic. Be glad for these wonderful memories, what a woman.
